newsitem.title: USA: Andrea says Northrop deal might not proceed.
newsitem.headline: Andrea says Northrop deal might not proceed.

text.p: Andrea Electronics Corp said it could not guarantee that it would go ahead with a supply agreement for its headsets with Northrop Grumman Corp because the gear was still undergoing quality testing.
Andrea said in a statement it expected initial qualification testing of its Active Noise Reduction/Active Noise Cancellation headsets to end this year.
A second required phase of testing, which could take at least nine months, would then be undertaken, it said.
"The company believes that a supply agreement, if any, would not be executed until completion of the second phase of testing," it said.
Northrop, a major defense and electronics company, has exclusive worldwide rights to market the headsets to U.S. military and non-U.S. military markets.

"Given the uncertainties inherent in the product qualification testing process and the ultimate price/performance characteristics of the company's headsets, the company has not made any projections as to the amount of sales revenue, if any, that it would derive from the sale of these products for military use," it said.
Andrea Electronics Corp makes audio communications equipment for the personal computer, telecommunications, military electronics and commercial markets.
Andrea shares were off 3-1/8 to 23-3/8 in American Stock Exchange trading.
